Assume AC. Every proper complex algebraic variety $Y$ admits a split simplicial
proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ with every $Y_p$ smooth projective. Here
proper hypercover means that $Y_0\to Y$ and each map
$Y_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}Y_\bullet)_p$ is proper and surjective. Two
such systems admit a third smooth projective proper hypercover mapping to both
over $Y$. Every morphism between proper varieties can be lifted to a morphism
between such hypercovers after refining the source. Degree-$n$ cohomology uses
only the finite skeleton through degree $n+1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives
$$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$
There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.

(i) Let $K$ be a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex
([[def-cohomological-mixed-hodge-complex]]). Then for every $n$ the vector
space $H^n(K_{\mathbb Q})$ carries a mixed Hodge structure whose weight
filtration is the shifted image filtration
$W_mH^n(K)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$ and whose Hodge
filtration is the image filtration
$F^pH^n(K_{\mathbb C})=\operatorname{im}(H^n(F^pK_{\mathbb C})\to H^n(K_{\mathbb C}))$.
In the weight spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-p}K)$
one has $E_1^{p,q}$ pure of weight $q$, the sequence degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(K)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ compatibly with the Hodge
filtrations. A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge complexes induces, on
every $H^n$, a morphism of the resulting mixed Hodge structures.

(ii) Let $K^\bullet$ be a cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge
complexes concentrated in nonnegative cohomological degrees: cochain complexes
$K^{p,q}$ with coface maps and an internal differential satisfying the
cosimplicial identities, with $K^{p,q}=0$ unless $p,q\ge0$, whose differentials
are strict for the Hodge filtration, and with $H^q(K^p)$, together with the
induced $F$ and the rational comparison, a pure Hodge structure of weight $q$
for all $p,q$ (the axioms (GH1)-(GH2) of a cohomological Hodge complex of
weight zero). Form its simple
complex $sK$ with the standard total differential and the increasing filtration
$L$ by cosimplicial degree, $L_{-p}sK^n=\bigoplus_{i\ge p}K^{i,n-i}$. Then $sK$
is a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex for the filtration $L$ and the
Hodge filtrations of the $K^p$, the cosimplicial spectral sequence
$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(K^p)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(sK)$ degenerates at $E_2$, and
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)\cong E_2^{n-q,q}$; consequently all weights of
$H^n(sK)$ are at most $n$.

A **rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex** consists of

(a) a bounded-below cochain complex $K_{\mathbb Q}$ of $\mathbb Q$-vector
spaces with an increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes, finite on each
cochain group;

(b) a cochain complex $K_{\mathbb C}$ of $\mathbb C$-vector spaces with an
increasing filtration $W$ by subcomplexes and a decreasing filtration $F$ by
subcomplexes, again finite on each cochain group;

(c) a morphism of complexes
$\alpha\colon K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$
compatible with the weight filtrations, such that for every $w$ the induced map
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_w\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism,

subject to the following axiom: for every integer $w$ the weight-graded
complex $\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK$ has finite-dimensional cohomology, its
differential (induced by $d_K$) is strict for the induced filtration $F$, and
for every $r$ the induced filtration $F$ on
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, together with the induced rational
comparison
$H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb Q})\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C\to
H^r(\operatorname{Gr}^W_wK_{\mathbb C})$, is a pure Hodge structure of weight
$r+w$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]).

Here a cochain complex is a complex in the sense of
[[def-cochain-complex-in-an-abelian-category]], a filtration by subcomplexes is
a filtered complex in the sense of [[def-filtered-chain-complex]], a morphism
compatible with the weight filtrations is a filtered chain map in the sense of
[[def-filtered-chain-map]], quasi-isomorphism means
[[def-quasi-isomorphism]], and finiteness on a cochain group $K^n$ means
$W_aK^n=0$ for all sufficiently negative $a$ and $W_aK^n=K^n$ for all
sufficiently positive $a$, with bounds depending on $n$; dually $F^pK^n=K^n$
for $p\ll0$ and $F^pK^n=0$ for $p\gg0$.

**The weight filtration on cohomology** is the shifted image filtration
$$W_mH^n(K):=\operatorname{im}\bigl(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K)\bigr).$$
The shift is essential: it is what makes the axiom's weight $r+w$ on the graded
complexes compatible with the weight of $H^n$, and pole-count weight on a
logarithmic complex is not the weight on its cohomology. The differential
strictness in the axiom is Deligne's condition (GH1); the equivalent
formulation that the $F$-spectral sequence of the graded complex degenerates at
its first page is recorded in the sources but is neither asserted nor used
here, so no degeneration theorem enters this definition.

**Morphisms and the sheaf case.** A morphism of cohomological mixed Hodge
complexes is a pair of chain maps $K_{\mathbb Q}\to L_{\mathbb Q}$ and
$K_{\mathbb C}\to L_{\mathbb C}$ compatible with both filtrations and with the
comparisons; compatible filtered homotopies are permitted. The same
definitions apply to bounded-below complexes of sheaves on a topological space
when the complexes are replaced by their derived global sections and the
resolutions used preserve the graded pieces; the existence of such resolutions
for the concrete complexes used later is proved where those complexes are
constructed, not here.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de
Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and
$$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$
Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth
representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the
Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the
kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms),
$H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration
$F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration
induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose
spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$.
Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product
preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge
structure.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
Jacobian-criterion, ample-powers, Chern-form and comparison suppliers below.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$.

Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **complex manifold**
$X^{\mathrm{an}}$, its **analytification**: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$
this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex
dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the
finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the
convention of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if
$X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth
algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and
every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$.

Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth
positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham
class is the real image of the topological first Chern class
$c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$:
$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.

Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for
$W$ and for $F$:
$$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$
for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient
filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is
exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is
$W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has
pure image of weight $n$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a quasi-projective complex algebraic variety, $k$ a
field, and $F$ a bounded complex of analytic $k$-sheaves whose cohomology is
locally constant of finite rank on a finite complex algebraic stratification.
Fix finitely many algebraic supports and locally closed inclusions to be
respected. There is a finite compatible smooth complex algebraic Whitney
refinement, a projective compactification with its algebraic boundary
respected, and a finite pair of simplicial complexes $(K,D)$ such that
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\cong|K|\setminus|D|$, every open simplex lies in one complex
stratum, and the marked supports are unions of simplices. One can take
$\dim K\le2\dim_{\mathbb C}X$; in particular constant-sheaf cohomology vanishes
above that real dimension. The same construction applies individually to the
compact controlled links supplied by the conical-neighborhood theorem.

On these models, actual ordinary and compact-support cohomology, ordinary
derived Hom, internal derived Hom and local cohomology with a prescribed
algebraic support have bounded finite-dimensional cochain models. Internal Hom
is constructible on a finite complex Whitney refinement. The local link and
support models vary locally constantly along the corresponding complex strata;
thus their cohomology has finite rank there. Every such model commutes with
extension of the coefficient field. Inclusions and supports are chosen in
finite collections for a given construction; no compatible triangulation of
arbitrary algebraic maps or cyclic diagrams is asserted. Perverse dimensions
remain the dimensions of the complex strata, independent of the auxiliary real
simplices.

Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and let $\sigma$ be a nonempty simplex.
Let $\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma$ be the subcomplex of simplices $\tau$ disjoint
from $\sigma$ with $\sigma\cup\tau\in K$, and let $\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)$
be the open star of $\sigma$
([[def-simplicial-subcomplex-star-closure-and-link]]). Then
$$\operatorname{st}_K(\sigma)\cong\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(|\operatorname{lk}_K\sigma|),$$
where $c_{<1}(L)=(L\times[0,1))/(L\times\{0\})$ with the quotient topology, and
the cone on the empty space means a single apex. The homeomorphism takes each
simplex interior containing $\sigma$ to the product with the corresponding
link-simplex interior and positive radial coordinate; the simplex $\sigma$
itself maps to the apex. The link is compact and has finitely many simplices.
If $D\subseteq K$ is a subcomplex and $\sigma\notin D$, this star lies in
$|K|\setminus|D|$.

Let $X$ be a classical algebraic variety over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]: a separated
quasi-compact locally ringed space over $\mathbb C$ with a finite cover by
affine models $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the morphisms being the regular maps,
i.e. the morphisms of locally ringed spaces over $\mathbb C$
([[def-morphism-locally-ringed-spaces]]).

(a) **Analytic topology.** An affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ carries the
subspace topology of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb C^n$
([[lem-metrics-on-rn]], [[def-metric-topology]],
[[rem-complex-euclidean-space-dictionary]],
[[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). If $Z_1,Z_2\subseteq X$ are affine
models and $\varphi:Z_1\to Z_2$ is the structure-sheaf isomorphism, then on
$Z_1\cap Z_2$ the maps $\varphi$ and $\varphi^{-1}$ are given locally by
polynomial quotient functions
([[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]) and are
therefore continuous for the Euclidean topologies: polynomial functions are
continuous, and a quotient is continuous wherever its denominator does not
vanish ([[lem-algebra-of-continuous-real-maps-on-a-space]],
[[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]]). Hence the topologies transported
from the two affine models agree on the overlap, so the affine-model topologies
glue to a unique topology on the underlying set of $X$
([[def-topological-space]], [[def-subspace-topology-top]]): the **analytic
topology** of $X$. Every regular map of complex classical varieties is
continuous for the analytic topologies, by the same local description
([[def-continuous-map-top]]), and the analytic topology refines the Zariski
topology because polynomial zero sets are Euclidean closed. Whenever a complex
algebraic variety is used as a topological space below it carries the analytic
topology, and each subvariety carries the subspace topology.

(b) **Smooth points.** Let $S$ be a classical variety over $\mathbb C$ and let
$x\in S$. The point $x$ is a **smooth point of $S$** if its algebraic local ring
$\mathcal O_{S,x}$ is a regular local ring: a nonzero Noetherian local ring
whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_x$ satisfies
$\dim_{\mathbb C}(\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2)=\dim\mathcal O_{S,x}$
([[def-embedding-dimension-and-regular-local-ring]]). The residue field at a
classical complex point is $\mathbb C$. The variety $S$ is **smooth** if every
point is smooth. This intrinsic algebraic condition does not require a Zariski
neighbourhood to be algebraically isomorphic to an open subset of affine space.

(c) **Finite smooth algebraic stratifications.** A **finite smooth algebraic
stratification with the frontier condition** of $X$ is a finite decomposition
$X=\coprod_{\alpha\in A}S_\alpha$ into pairwise disjoint nonempty connected
locally closed subsets $S_\alpha\subseteq X$ — the **strata** — such that each
$S_\alpha$, with its reduced induced algebraic structure, is a smooth algebraic
subvariety of $X$; and such that for every $\alpha$ the closure
$\overline{S_\alpha}$ of $S_\alpha$ in $X$ is a union of strata. The latter is
the **frontier condition**: the frontier
$\overline{S_\alpha}\setminus S_\alpha$ of every stratum is a union of strata
([[def-connected-space]], [[def-interior-closure-boundary-top]]).

**The induced structure is the polynomial-quotient function sheaf, not a
restriction of $\mathcal O_X$.** A locally closed $S\subseteq X$ is, locally
inside an affine model $Z\subseteq\mathbb C^n$, the set of points with $h\neq0$
and $f_1=\dots=f_r=0$ for polynomials $h,f_1,\dots,f_r$ on $Z$
([[def-constructible-subset-variety]],
[[def-classical-algebraic-prevariety-regular-maps-and-varieties]]); the map
$z\mapsto(z,1/h(z))$ identifies it with the affine model
$\{(z,t):th(z)=1,\ f_1(z)=\dots=f_r(z)=0\}\subseteq\mathbb C^{n+1}$, and its
**reduced induced structure sheaf** is the one transported along this
identification: locally functions of the form $a/b$ with $b$ nonvanishing on the
set. The ambient restriction $\mathcal O_X|_S$ is not used, since already at the
origin of the affine line the ambient stalk is the local ring of the line while
the stalk of the reduced point is $\mathbb C$. An open subset of an affine model
is a union of principal open subsets, and each principal open subset is again an
affine model, so every locally closed subvariety of $X$ is a classical variety
for the induced structure sheaf. No existence theorem for stratifications, no
common-refinement theorem and no choice principle is asserted: nothing is
selected, and all cited suppliers are choice-free.

Let $X$ be a compact ([[def-compact-space]]) Hausdorff
([[def-hausdorff-space]]) topological space. Then:

1. $X$ is **regular** ([[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]]);
2. $X$ is **normal** ([[def-normal-and-t4-spaces]]);
3. $X$ is $T_1$ ([[def-t0-and-t1-spaces]]), and hence $X$ is $T_3$ and $T_4$.

Following [[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]] and [[def-normal-and-t4-spaces]],
*regular* and *normal* name the separation conditions alone and the numerals
$T_3$ and $T_4$ name their conjunctions with $T_1$; claim 3 is what supplies the
$T_1$ half, and it is stated separately for that reason.

**Nothing stronger is claimed.** In particular it is not asserted here that a
compact Hausdorff space is completely regular
([[def-regular-and-t3-spaces]] distinguishes the two conditions), and no
continuous real-valued function is produced anywhere below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice. Every open cover
of a compact Hausdorff space admits a finite partition of unity subordinate to
that cover.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

Let $X$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological space and let $R$ be a
commutative ring. For $k\ge0$ let $S_k(X)$ be the set of continuous maps
$\Delta^k\to X$ from the standard simplex
([[def-singular-simplex-and-singular-chain-group-with-coefficients]]); the
convention of [[lem-a-locally-compact-hausdorff-space-has-a-base-of-open-sets-with-compact-closure]]
supplies neighbourhood bases by open sets with compact closure. A formal sum
$c=\sum_{\sigma\in S_k(X)}a_\sigma\,\sigma$ with $a_\sigma\in R$ is **locally
finite** if every point $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood meeting only
finitely many of the images $\sigma(\Delta^k)$ of the simplices with
$a_\sigma\ne0$ ([[def-compact-space]] for compactness). The **locally finite
$k$-chains** are the $R$-module
$$C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)=\bigl\{c:\ \text{the sum is locally finite}\bigr\},\qquad C_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)=0\ \ (k<0),$$
with addition and scalar multiplication defined coefficientwise. The **boundary**
$$\partial\Bigl(\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\sigma\Bigr)=\sum_\sigma a_\sigma\,\partial\sigma$$
is again locally finite, because every face of $\sigma$ has image contained in
the image of $\sigma$, and $\partial^2=0$ because $\partial^2\sigma=0$; thus
$(C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R),\partial)$ is a chain complex and its homology is the
**Borel-Moore homology** $H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)$
([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]] for the ordinary chain
complex, which is the special case of sums with finite support).

A **proper** continuous map $f:X\to Y$ (inverse images of compact sets are
compact) induces $f_*:C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\to C_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y;R)$ by
$\sigma\mapsto f\circ\sigma$: for $y\in Y$ choose a compact neighbourhood $K$
of $y$; the compact set $f^{-1}(K)$ is covered by finitely many of the
neighbourhoods furnished by local finiteness of $c$, so only finitely many
simplices meet $f^{-1}(K)$, and a neighbourhood of $y$ contained in $K$ then
meets only finitely many images $f(\sigma(\Delta^k))$. This is a chain map
because $f\circ\partial\sigma=\partial(f\circ\sigma)$, so it induces
$f_*:H_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\to H_*^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y;R)$. Coefficients and degree
are otherwise unused below. No choice principle is used in the definition; a
homeomorphism and, more generally, a proper continuous map act functorially.

Let $X$ be a compact Hausdorff topological space and let $R$ be a commutative
ring. The inclusion of the ordinary singular chain complex into the complex of
locally finite chains of [[def-borel-moore-homology]] is an isomorphism of chain
complexes, and it induces isomorphisms
$$H_k^{\mathrm{BM}}(X;R)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_k^{\mathrm{sing}}(X;R)$$
in every degree, natural for continuous maps of compact Hausdorff spaces
([[def-singular-chain-complex-and-singular-homology]]). In particular the class
map of a proper complex algebraic variety may be computed using ordinary
singular homology.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

For continuous $f:X\to Y$, $\alpha\in H^p(Y;R)$ and $x\in H_n(X;R)$,
$$f_*(f^*\alpha\cap x)=\alpha\cap f_*x.$$
For $\alpha\in H^p(X;R)$, $\beta\in H^q(X;R)$ and $x\in H_n(X;R)$,
$$(\alpha\smile\beta)\cap x=\beta\cap(\alpha\cap x).$$
Here $R$ is commutative unital and cap evaluates the front face, retaining the back face. Both identities hold already on cochains and chains. No AC is needed.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: (Actual cosimplicial Hodge complexes.) Choose the smooth projective proper hypercover $a:Y_\bullet\to Y$ of [F1]. Use the exact functorial Godement construction of [F7], applied on every $Y_p$, and put $K_{\mathbb Q}^{p,q}=\Gamma(Y_p,C^q(\mathbb Q_{Y_p}))$ and $K_{\mathbb C}^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{k+t=q}\Gamma(Y_p,C^t(\Omega^k_{Y_p}))$, for $p,q\ge0$, with $F^b$ given by $k\ge b$. These are the resolved global de Rham complexes, not the complex of global holomorphic forms. Godement pullback along each face is induced by pulling a germ collection at a point to the stalk over its image; the successive cokernels preserve these maps, so their composites obey the simplicial identities and preserve $F$. The constant inclusion $\mathbb Q\otimes\mathbb C\to\Omega^0$ gives the functorial rational comparison; on cohomology it is the scalar-extension comparison of [F4]. Exactness and acyclicity of the resolution show $H^q(K_{\mathbb C}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb C)$, with the holomorphic-degree image filtration, and $H^q(K_{\mathbb Q}^p)=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$. The compact Hodge theorem [F4] gives pure weight $q$ and Hodge-de Rham $E_1$ degeneration on each smooth projective component. The latter makes the actual internal differential $F$-strict: if $dx\in F^b$, degeneration lifts the leading lower-filtration class of $x$ to a cycle up to a higher-filtration term and a boundary; subtracting the cycle and boundary raises the preimage filtration without changing $dx$, and finite induction supplies a preimage in $F^b$, as in the strict correction of [F7]. Thus every level is an actual weight-zero rational Hodge complex. Each internal total diagonal is finite, and $F^{q+1}K^{p,q}=0$, so [F3] applies to its first-quadrant simple complex, giving the mixed Hodge structure and $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(Y_p;\mathbb Q)$, $E_2$ degeneration and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_qH^n(sK)=E_2^{n-q,q}$. The terms have $p=n-q\ge0$, so weights are at most $n$, and the finitely many terms on every total diagonal are finite-dimensional by [F4]. Descent [F2] identifies the rational simple cohomology naturally with $H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$, carrying this structure.

Identify the descended cohomology with ordinary singular cohomology of the analytic space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ [F6]. The space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact: $Y_0\to Y$ is proper and surjective and $Y_0$ is smooth projective, so $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}$ is compact by [F4] and its image under the continuous surjection $Y_0^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ is all of the compact space $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$; it is Hausdorff and second-countable in the analytic topology [F6]. For the local contractibility hypothesis of [F6], cover $Y$ by finitely many affine charts, each quasi-projective, and apply the triangulation theorem and the conical-star lemma of [F6] chartwise: at a point in the relative interior of a retained simplex $\sigma$, its open star is a neighbourhood with chart $\operatorname{relint}|\sigma|\times c_{<1}(L)$ taking the point to $(p,\mathrm{apex})$. Shrink the first factor to convex open neighbourhoods of $p$ and the second to cones of radius $0<\epsilon<1$. Compactness of $L$ gives uniform radial neighbourhoods at the apex, so these products form a neighbourhood basis; each is contractible by straight-line contraction of the first factor and radial contraction of the cone. The same basis restricted to any open subset proves its local contractibility. Metrizability is obtained from the cutoffs of [F6]: compactness and normality give finitely many chart pieces and continuous cutoff functions equal to one on each piece and supported in its affine chart, the products of the cutoffs with the coordinate functions give a continuous injection of the compact space into Hausdorff Euclidean space, and the induced metric has the analytic topology. The sheaf-singular comparison of [F6] then identifies $H^n(Y^{\mathrm{an}},\mathbb Q_{\mathrm{const}})\cong H^n_{\mathrm{sing}}(Y^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Q)$, and the mixed Hodge structure of step 1.1 is carried to $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$; the only choice used is the dependent choice for the partition of unity, supplied from AC by [F6].

Independence and functoriality. If $a':Y'_\bullet\to Y$ is a second split proper hypercover with smooth projective terms, [F1] supplies a third such hypercover dominating both; the two refinements give filtered comparison maps between the corresponding cosimplicial systems and hence morphisms of the mixed Hodge complexes of step 1.1, and by [F2] both simple complexes compute the constant-sheaf cohomology of $Y$, so the induced maps on $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ are the identity; strictness [F5] upgrades this to an isomorphism of mixed Hodge structures, so the structure is independent of the diagram. A morphism $g:Y\to Y'$ of proper varieties lifts, after refining the source hypercover, to a morphism of the chosen hypercovers [F1], pullback of holomorphic forms along it is a morphism of the cosimplicial mixed Hodge complexes compatible with the comparisons, and independence of the hypercovers makes the induced map $g^*:H^n(Y',\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ well defined and compatible with identities and composition.

(The smooth-open clause and the actual total map.) Let $g:Y\to U$ and choose the logarithmic comparison model on $X\supset U$ from [F7]. Define its pullback into the simple complex of step 1.1 to be supported in cosimplicial degree zero, using $g_0=ga_0:Y_0\to U$. Pullback of a logarithmic form is regular on $Y_0$: a boundary equation pulls back to a nowhere-zero holomorphic function, whose $d\log$ is regular. Apply the functorial Godement resolutions to obtain the internal chain map into $K_{\mathbb C}^{0,*}$ preserving holomorphic degree. Its first alternating face differential is zero, since $g_0d_0=g_0d_1$ on $Y_1$, so this degree-zero-supported map is an actual chain map into the simple total complex; no map into every positive cosimplicial degree is being implicitly summed. On the rational side the natural pullback from $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ along $jg_0$, with the augmentation comparison, gives the same degree-zero-supported map, and it is compatible with the logarithmic meridian comparison up to the permitted filtered homotopies. For weight indices $a<0$ the source pole filtration is zero; for $a\ge0$ the target $L_a$ is the whole first-quadrant simple complex, so the map preserves weights. It preserves $F$ by form degree. Thus it is a morphism of the mixed Hodge complexes, and descent identifies its cohomology map with the actual rational pullback $g^*:H^n(U;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(Y;\mathbb Q)$. The functoriality clause of [F3] makes this a mixed Hodge morphism.

The class map. Let $h:Y\to X$ be proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, so $Y^{\mathrm{an}}$ and $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ are compact and the Borel-Moore homology of $Y$ agrees with ordinary singular homology by [F8]. Give $H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)$ the dual of the mixed Hodge structure on $H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$. For the dual filtrations in [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], finite-dimensional linear algebra identifies $\operatorname{Gr}^W_a(H^*)$ with $(\operatorname{Gr}^W_{-a}H)^*$; annihilator Hodge filtrations negate each pure type $(p,q)$ to $(-p,-q)$, so these pieces are pure of weight $a$ and the dual is a mixed Hodge structure. Its weights are at least $-i$. Transposing a filtration-preserving map preserves the annihilator filtrations, so dual pullbacks are mixed Hodge morphisms. The pushforward $h_*:H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\to H_i(X,\mathbb Q)$ is dual, under the Kronecker pairings of [F8], to the pullback $h^*:H^i(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^i(Y,\mathbb Q)$, which is a mixed Hodge morphism by step 3.1; hence $h_*$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the dual structures. Poincare duality for the compact oriented manifold $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ and the compatibility of cap product with the cup product and the trace [F8] identify $H_i(X,\mathbb Q)\cong H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$ as pure Hodge structures of weight $-i$, the fundamental class having type $(d,d)$ so that the Tate twist removes the shift. Composing the pushforward with this identification, the class map $H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\to H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism from a structure of weights at least $-i$ to the pure structure of weight $-i$, so by [F5] its image is a pure Hodge substructure of weight $-i$; untwisting, the image in $H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)$ is a pure Hodge substructure of weight $2d-i$. No smoothness of $Y$ was used.

Boundaries and Choice accounting. For $Y=\varnothing$ every group is zero with the trivial structure and all clauses are vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case has all weights equal to $0$, consistent with the bound; the reducible and mixed-dimensional case is handled componentwise in [F4]; and the case $Y=X$ with $d=\dim X$ reduces the class map to Poincare duality itself. The Axiom of Choice [F9] is inherited from [F1], [F2] and [F7], and is used exactly once more as dependent choice for the subordinate partition of unity in step 2.1, supplied by [F6].

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex
algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with weights at most $n$. For a
morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback
$H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on
$U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, the
proper homological class map
$$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$
is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and
consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure.
No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed.

Every morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for
$W$ and for $F$:
$$f(W_nH)=f(H)\cap W_nK,\qquad f(F^pH_{\mathbb C})=f(H_{\mathbb C})\cap F^pK_{\mathbb C}$$
for all $n,p$. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with the induced or quotient
filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; the functor $\operatorname{Gr}^W_n$ is
exact; and a morphism from a structure of weights at least $n$ (that is
$W_{n-1}H=0$) to a structure of weights at most $n$ (that is $W_nK=K$) has
pure image of weight $n$.

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Conjugation.** The $\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the sums of subspaces are those of the complexifications, and the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: By [F3] applied to the mixed Hodge morphism $g^*$ and the strictness identity $g^*(W_nH^n(U))=\operatorname{im}g^*\cap W_nH^n(Y)$, the target weight bound $W_nH^n(Y)=H^n(Y)$ of [F2] reduces the right-hand side to $\operatorname{im}g^*$; by [F1] the image of $W_nH^n(U)$ under $g^*$ is $g^*(\operatorname{im}j^*)=\operatorname{im}(g^*j^*)=\operatorname{im}((jg)^*)$. Hence the two asserted images agree as actual subspaces of $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$, without choosing a splitting of the weight filtration on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$.

Put $I=\operatorname{im}g^*$. Strictness gives $W_{n-1}I=g^*(W_{n-1}H^n(U))$, and by [F1] the source has weights at least $n$, so $W_{n-1}I=0$; the target bound gives $W_nI=I$. Hence the induced mixed Hodge structure on $I$ is pure of weight $n$, and by step 1.1 the image of $(jg)^*$ is the same pure substructure.

Boundaries and Choice accounting. If $U=\varnothing$ or $Y=\varnothing$ all groups vanish and the claim is vacuous; the degree $n=0$ case gives weight-zero images by the same strictness argument; the case $U=X$ has $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $W_nH^n(U)=H^n(U)$, so both images are the full image of $g^*$, consistent with the statement; and $Y$ smooth or reduced is not required, the target bound being the only hypothesis on the target. The Axiom of Choice [F4] is inherited from [F1] and [F2]; no selection is made in this argument.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $C$ be an integral projective curve over a
perfect field $k$. Then its normalization $C^{\nu}$ is a nonsingular projective
curve, and $\nu\colon C^{\nu}\to C$ is a finite birational morphism.
Consequently every integral projective curve over a perfect field admits a
nonsingular projective model.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite morphism of schemes is proper. No
Noetherian, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is used, the empty morphism
and the zero ring are included, and the Axiom of Choice enters only through the
universal closedness of finite morphisms.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives
$$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$
There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.

Assume AC. The rational cohomology $H^n(Y,\mathbb Q)$ of every proper complex
algebraic variety has a functorial mixed Hodge structure
([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]) with weights at most $n$. For a
morphism $g:Y\to U$ with $Y$ proper and $U$ smooth quasiprojective, its pullback
$H^n(U)\to H^n(Y)$ is a mixed Hodge morphism for the logarithmic structure on
$U$. If $Y\to X$ is proper with $X$ smooth projective of dimension $d$, the
proper homological class map
$$H_i^{\mathrm{BM}}(Y,\mathbb Q)=H_i(Y,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^{2d-i}(X,\mathbb Q)(d)$$
is a mixed Hodge morphism after the indicated Tate twist. Its image, and
consequently the untwisted image in $H^{2d-i}(X)$, is a pure Hodge substructure.
No smoothness of $Y$ is assumed.

Let
$$S^2:=\{(x,y,t)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+t^2=1\}.$$
Define
$$\Sigma(z)=\left(\frac{2\operatorname{Re}z}{1+|z|^2},\ \frac{2\operatorname{Im}z}{1+|z|^2},\ \frac{|z|^2-1}{1+|z|^2}\right)\qquad(z\in\mathbb C)$$
and $\Sigma(\infty)=(0,0,1)$. Then $\Sigma:\widehat{\mathbb C}\to S^2$ is a
homeomorphism, with inverse
$$\Pi(x,y,t)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x+iy}{1-t},&(x,y,t)\neq(0,0,1),\\ \infty,&(x,y,t)=(0,0,1).\end{cases}$$

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas
$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

derivations.claim: The Cech nerve $C_\bullet$ of the normalization has degree-$p$ term $C_p=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup T_p$, where $T_p$ consists of the $2^{p+1}-2$ isolated points indexed by the nonconstant tuples in $\{a,b\}^{p+1}$: over the node the fibre product of copies of $\nu$ has one reduced point per tuple of preimages, and over the smooth locus it is the diagonal copy of $\mathbb P^1$ [F1]. Each $C_p$ is therefore a finite disjoint union of a smooth projective curve and reduced points, hence smooth projective, and the matching maps of the Cech nerve are base changes and finite products of the finite surjection $\nu$, hence proper and surjective, so $C_\bullet\to C$ is a proper hypercover to which [F2] applies. Taking cohomology gives $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C_p,\mathbb Q)$, which vanishes for $q\ge1$ except in degree two where it is $\mathbb Q$ on the diagonal component; on the degree-zero row $E_1^{p,0}=H^0(C_p,\mathbb Q)$ is the direct sum of one copy of $\mathbb Q$ for the diagonal and one for each nonconstant tuple.

Compute the degree-zero row in low degrees. On $C_0=\mathbb P^1$ one has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q$, and on $C_1=\mathbb P^1_d\sqcup\{ab\}\sqcup\{ba\}$ one has $E_1^{1,0}=\mathbb Q_d\oplus\mathbb Q_{ab}\oplus\mathbb Q_{ba}$; the alternating sum of the two face pullbacks $\delta^0$ sends a constant to the differences of the two diagonal values, hence is zero. On $C_2$ the six nonconstant tuples contribute the coordinates for $(aab),(aba),(abb),(baa),(bab),(bba)$, and evaluating the alternating sum $\delta^1(c)$ on these components and on the diagonal gives $c_d$ on $(aab),(abb),(baa),(bba)$ and $c_{ab}+c_{ba}$ on $(aba),(bab)$, where $c=(c_d,c_{ab},c_{ba})$. Hence $\delta^1(c)=0$ exactly when $c_d=0$ and $c_{ba}=-c_{ab}$, so $E_2^{1,0}=\ker\delta^1/\operatorname{im}\delta^0$ is one-dimensional, generated by $(0,1,-1)$.

The other total-degree-one entry is $E_1^{0,1}=H^1(\mathbb P^1,\mathbb Q)=0$ by [F3], so it contributes nothing; the spectral sequence is first-quadrant with finite diagonals and degenerates at $E_2$ by [F2]. Therefore $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)\cong E_2^{1,0}$ is one-dimensional, and by the weight identification of [F2] its graded pieces are $\operatorname{Gr}^W_0H^1=E_2^{1,0}=\mathbb Q$ and $\operatorname{Gr}^W_1H^1=E_2^{0,1}=0$. Since the weights of $H^1(C,\mathbb Q)$ are at most $1$, this forces $W_0H^1=H^1$: the whole one-dimensional space is pure of weight $0$ and type $(0,0)$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), as asserted.
